pairs.why: B's stack is centered and fills the card with a tight, even margin like the real map stack, though both are close.
A's locomotive is large and cropped by the left and bottom edges like the real close-up bus and coaster cards, while B is a smaller whole object with a lot of sky.
Both rovers have almost the same scale, placement and margins, so composition gives no reason to choose.
A's glass fills most of the card height and width like the real glass, while B's smaller glass leaves too much empty purple around it.
A's canopy spans the card and its pole runs nearly to the bottom edge, matching the real umbrella's hero scale and diagonal, while B is slightly more compact.
B's calculator has the stronger diagonal tilt and the same generous margins as the real one, while A is more upright and crowds the top and bottom.
A's slide fills the card to the edges and is cropped by the bottom pool edge like the real card, while B is smaller with more margin.
B is a wall clock that floats on the stripes with the same size and margins as the real one, while A has a floor and shadow band the real card lacks.
